title: ASIC bans adviser over Shield super scandal
full_text:
The corporate regulator has imposed a four-year ban on one of the financial advisers linked to the Shield Master Fund after finding he failed to act in the best interests of clients, provided inappropriate advice and made false statements.
Former MWL Financial Services financial adviser Pardeep Singh will be unable to provide financial services until mid 2030 and is now on the banned and disqualified register after unsuccessfully applying to a tribunal for the action against him to not be made public.
During his time at MWL, Mr Singh recommended clients roll over their super into Shield’s growth and high-growth classes, according to the Australian Securities & Investments Commission. These classes were high risk and had no track record.
As well, statements of advice (SOAs) provided by Mr Singh contained false or materially misleading statements regarding Shield’s historical performance, according to the regulator.
The SOAs included comparisons, projections and graphs suggesting Shield had generated returns and outperformed alternative products since 2016, despite Shield only being in operation from May 2021. ASIC found those statements were likely to persuade clients to go ahead with his recommendations.
Mr Singh worked under MWL’s licence from September 2023 to December 2024 before he moved to another licensee caught up in the same scandal, InterPrac Financial Planning. He stayed with InterPrac until April 2026 and his ban took effect the following month.
ASIC has now banned more than a dozen MWL advisers, as well as its former head of compliance and managing director, Nicholas Maikousis, in the wake of the Shield scandal that cost 5800 investors about $500bn.
The advice firm tipped hundreds of clients’ super savings into the Shield fund before it collapsed into liquidation in 2024. ASIC is suing MWL over its role in the scandal, alleging in court that between mid 2022 and early 2024, MWL advisers recommended Shield to more than 550 clients.
